newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Senator says Trump disguised campaign gifts.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Senator says Trump disguised campaign gifts.

text.p: A New York State Senator said Monday that Donald Trump, the real estate mogul, might have violated election laws by funneling $130,000 of campaign contributions to Republicans through his wife, Marla Maples.

Franz Leichter (D-Manhattan) said Maples gave the money to two political actions committees that he said apparantly were created this year to disguise Trump's gifts. Another $15,000 was contributed by Trump's top lobbyist, Albert Pirro.
If Maples did not contribute her own money, and if Pirro was reimbursed by Trump, "Then the law has clearly been violated," Leichter wrote, in prepared comments.
Martin McLaughlin, a spokesman for Trump, called Leichters' comments "sexist," adding "She's an independent voter and makes her own decisions." He also said Leichter owed Maples an apology.

Leichter said his analysis of state Board of Election filings showed that Trump made a total of at least $246,100 in contributions to state political action committees and candidates in 1995 and 1996.

"It appears that Donald Trump is set on buying the legislature," said Leichter. He noted Trump's businesses would be affected by several issues pending before the legislature, including a constitutional amendment to allow casino gambling and a plan to provide $345 million of tax-exempt bonds for Trump's Riverside South development in Manhattan.
Trump is chairman of Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts.
